title: Juniper and the Letter
premise: In the winter of 1934, Wren Nakamura keeps the light at Juniper Point, a widowed mother measuring her life in what can be carried. When the season's storms close the tidal bridge and a dying fisherman presses a packet of letters into her hands — proof that the cannery owner has been falsifying wreck reports to collect insurance on lost crews — she becomes an unwilling courier. Trapped between three checkpoints controlled by the man she must expose, Wren navigates loyalty to neighbors who depend on his wages, the truth about her husband's own drowning, and the memory of what survival has already cost her. She ends by choosing truth over safety, testifying as the bridge reopens, and relighting the lamp for ships that will finally be told the whole story.
about_author: Coral Montrose is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing coastal shipping records before turning to fiction. She writes from a converted keeper's cottage on the northern coast, where the fog still dictates her working hours.

chapters.title: The Weight of Small Things
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Establishes her ritual of inventorying what can be carried — oil, matches, her daughter's shoes — as the great storms begin. Emotional beat: grief worn down into competence.

chapters.title: A Man Against the Rocks
chapters.summary: Wren finds a half-drowned fisherman, Elias, washed below the light after a wreck the official log calls 'no casualties.' His POV briefly interleaves. Beat: dread disguised as duty.

chapters.title: The Packet
chapters.summary: Dying, Elias gives Wren letters proving cannery owner Aldous Crane falsified wreck reports for insurance money — including one naming her late husband's boat. Beat: the past cracking open.

chapters.title: The Bridge Closes
chapters.summary: The storm season closes the tidal bridge; the mainland is unreachable until spring. Wren realizes she is trapped with evidence everyone wants buried. Beat: claustrophobia.

chapters.title: What the Neighbors Owe
chapters.summary: Wren surveys the village: half the families owe their winter wages to Crane. Her closest friend, Marta, warns her quietly to burn the letters. Beat: loyalty pulling against truth.

chapters.title: First Checkpoint
chapters.summary: Crane's foreman Halvard searches all outbound boats at the cannery dock. Wren passes through carrying nothing — but learns he's looking for something specific. Beat: cold fear.

chapters.title: Her Husband's Logbook
chapters.summary: Reading her husband Toma's recovered logbook, Wren discovers he had found Crane's fraud before he drowned — and had planned to sail to the mainland himself. Beat: betrayal and terrible kinship.

chapters.title: Marta's Bargain
chapters.summary: Marta reveals Crane holds her family's debt; she offers to help Wren in exchange for silence afterward. Wren must decide whether trust can survive transaction. Beat: uneasy alliance.

chapters.title: The Second Checkpoint
chapters.summary: The harbor master, old Mr. Pell, owes Wren a debt from a rescue years ago but answers to Crane now. He looks away from her dory — then sends word that he saw nothing, twice. Beat: gratitude shadowed by danger.

chapters.title: Daughter of the Light
chapters.summary: Quiet interlude in Wren's POV with her daughter Noor, who has secretly read one of the letters. Mother and daughter negotiate what children are allowed to know. Beat: tenderness under pressure.

chapters.title: Halvard Comes Calling
chapters.summary: Halvard searches the lighthouse itself while Wren stalls him over tea. The letters hide inside the lens housing, inches from discovery. Beat: near-catastrophe.

chapters.title: The Storm That Took Toma
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter reconstructing the night Toma drowned — and revealing Crane ordered his boat out despite warnings. Beat: rage crystallizing into resolve.

chapters.title: A Third Road
chapters.summary: Elias, recovering slowly, remembers a smugglers' path around the headland usable only at low tide in calm weather — which the storms have not offered in weeks. Beat: hope rationed thin.

chapters.title: Pell's Confession
chapters.summary: The harbor master admits he signed false manifests for years and gives Wren the original manifest book — doubling her burden and her proof. Beat: complicity and courage entangled.

chapters.title: The Turn
chapters.summary: Crane, tipped off by an anonymous note, offers Wren a bribe: keepership for life, debts forgiven, if she hands over the papers. Beat: temptation measured against memory.

chapters.title: Refusal
chapters.summary: Wren refuses publicly at the cannery hall, forcing Crane to act openly. He seals the village, and Marta's help becomes treason. Beat: point of no return.

chapters.title: Low Tide, Rising Wind
chapters.summary: A brief calm window opens. Wren, Noor, and the documents set out along the smugglers' path as the weather turns behind them. Beat: desperate momentum.

chapters.title: Third Checkpoint
chapters.summary: At the far landing, Halvard waits, having guessed the route. Pell arrives and stands between them, finally spending his authority. Beat: sacrifice and standoff.

chapters.title: The Crossing
chapters.summary: Mid-crossing, the storm returns; Wren must choose between saving the packet and saving herself when the dory swamps. She lashed the letters to her body hours ago. Beat: climax of endurance.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: On the mainland, Wren delivers the evidence to the marine board; survivors' families arrive to corroborate. Crane's empire begins to crack. Beat: vindication without triumph.

chapters.title: Reckonings
chapters.summary: Spring returns; the bridge reopens. Marta faces her bargain, Halvard his choices, and Wren the fact that truth cost her neighbors dearly too. Beat: complicated forgiveness.

chapters.title: Juniper Light
chapters.summary: Final chapter: Wren relights the lamp after repairs, Noor beside her, the log open to a blank page. She writes the true account of every wreck. Beat: peace earned, memory kept.
